Rashi on Nedarim 35a:1:1.hebrew: ה"ג קונם פרה שאני הנאה לך - והכי משמע: קונם יהו עליך שאר פרות שיש לי שאני מהנה לך, כלומר שאין לי פרה אחרת וזו שיש לי איני משאילך — שזו לא רצה להשאילו והאחרות אסורות עליו בנדר — או שאמר לו: נכסי אסורין עליך אם יש לי פרה אחרת אלא זו, ונמצא שיש לו פרה אחרת, אסור לישאל ליהנות:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:1:1.english: This is the reading: Konam [be] a cow [by] which I benefit you - And this is what it means: Konam be upon you [any] other cows that I have [with] which I might benefit you — that is to say, [he claims] that I have no other cow, and this one that I have I will not lend you — for this one he did not want to lend him, and the others are forbidden to him by a vow. Or if he said to him: My property is forbidden to you if I have another cow besides this one, and it is found that he has another cow, it is forbidden [for him] to borrow [it] to benefit [from it].

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:1:2.hebrew: קונם קורדום שיש לי שאיני קנוי - כלומר, שלא קניתי קורדום אחר, וזה איני משאילך שאני צריך לו; או שאמר לו: קונם נכסי יהו אסורים עלי אם יש לי קורדום אחר אלא זה, ונמצא שיש לו קורדום אחר:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:1:2.english: Konam any spade that I have that I did not purchase - That is to say, [he meant] that I did not purchase another spade, and this one I am not lending to you because I need it; or he said to him: Konam, my property shall be forbidden to me if I have any spade other than this one, and it was found that he has another spade.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:1:3.hebrew: בחייו אסור - בעל הקורדום אסור ליהנות מנכסיו כל ימי חייו, אי נמי בחייו דמדיר אסורין נכסיו על המודר:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:1:3.english: During his lifetime [it] is forbidden - The owner of the spade is forbidden to benefit from his [own] property all the days of his life; or alternatively, during the lifetime of the one who made the vow, his property is forbidden to the subject of the vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:1:4.english: [He] died - [This refers to] the lender.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:1:5.hebrew: או שנתנה לו במתנה - למודר. אמר לן המורה: האי דקתני "מת" לא קאי אסיפא כלל, דהיכי מצי קתני אסיפא [דהא] קתני "נכסי עלי", "מת או שנתנה לו במתנה הרי זה מותר"? מי מותר?! הרי אנפשיה קאמר! אלא ארישא קתני, אהשאילני פרתך, שאם מת המדיר מותר בפרה או בנכסים של מדיר, דהא אמר "נכסי", ומאחר שמת לאו נכסיה דידיה אינון, והכא נמי אם ניתנו לו במתנה. ואמר לן המורה דכס"ג שאני הנאה שאינו קנוי, כינוי לשון בני אדם (שרי), דהכי היו נודרים בירושלים, ובנדרים הלך אחר לשון בני אדם, קתני שניתנו לו במתנה הרי זה מותר. וקשיא לרבא דאמר אע"ג דיהיב ליה במתנה אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:1:5.english: Or [if] it was given to him as a gift - to the subject of the vow. Our teacher told us: This [clause] that it teaches "he died" does not refer to the latter clause at all. For how could it teach regarding the latter clause, [since] it teaches "My property [is forbidden] to me," [and then] "he died or it was given to him as a gift, it is permitted"? How could it be permitted? Why, he spoke [the vow] against himself! Rather, it teaches [this] regarding the first clause, regarding "Lend me your cow," that if the vower died, [the subject of the vow] is permitted [to benefit] from the cow or from the property of the vower, because he said "my property," and once he died, it is no longer his property; and here too if it was given to him as a gift. And our teacher told us that in such a case, a benefit that is not acquired is different — [it is] an idiomatic expression of people's speech (it is permitted) — for thus they used to vow in Jerusalem, and in vows one follows the language of people; [therefore] it teaches that [if] it was given to him as a gift, it is permitted. And this is a difficulty for Rava, who said that even though he gave it to him as a gift, it is forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:2:1.hebrew: אמר לך רבא הכא במאי עסקינן כגון שניתנה לו על ידי אחר - שבעל הפרה נתנו לאחר, ואותו אחר נתנו לשואל. ולהכי מותר, שכבר הוציאה משאיל מרשותו כשנתנה לאחר. אבל היכא דאמר ליה "ככרי עליך", ולא נתנה לו על ידי אחר, הואיל ולא יצאת מרשותו קודם לכן, אסור. ולא דמי להיכא דאיגנבה מיניה, משום דהיכא דאיגנבה מיניה, הואיל ושלא מדעתו דבעל הככר יצא מרשותו, כעודה בידו דמי, ואסור. אבל היכא שנתנה לו במתנה על ידי אחר, יצאת מרשותו מדעתו:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:2:1.english: Rava would say to you: With what are we dealing here? For example, where it was given to him through another - [Meaning] that the owner of the cow gave it to another [person], and that other [person] gave it to the borrower. And therefore it is permitted, because the lender had already removed it from his possession when he gave it to the other [person]. However, where he said to him, "My loaf [is forbidden] to you," and did not give it to him through another, since it had not left his possession beforehand, it is forbidden. And it is not comparable to [the case] where it was stolen from him, because where it was stolen from him, since it left his possession without the consent of the owner of the loaf, it is considered as though it were still in his hand, and it is forbidden. But where he gave it to him as a gift through another, it left his possession with his consent.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:3:1.english: And it does not teach "that he gave it to him" - Which implies that he himself gave it to him.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:4:1.hebrew: יש מעילה בקונמות - היכא דאמר קונם ככר זה ואכלו, מי הוי כהקדש מעליא דיש בו מעילה ומעל, או לא:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:4:1.english: Is there misuse of consecrated property in [cases of] konamot - Where one said, "[May] this loaf [be] a konam," and ate it, is it like actual consecrated property, which is subject to misuse [of consecrated property], and [thus] he has committed misuse, or not?

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:5:1.hebrew: [תניתוה מקום] שנוטלין עליה שכר - ומודר היינו דאמר קונם, ומדמי ליה להקדש:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:5:1.english: [You learned: In a place] where one takes payment - And [the case of] one prohibited by a vow is [where] he said konam, and [the Mishnah] compares it to consecrated property.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:1.hebrew: קונם ככר זה הקדש - שאמר בלשון הקדש ובלשון קונם, והוא הדין נמי לא אמרה אלא בלשון קונם:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:1.english: This loaf is konam [like] consecrated property - That he stated [it] using the expression of "consecrated property" and using the expression of konam; and the same law also [applies if] he only stated it using the expression of konam.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:2.english: Whether he or another misused consecrated property - For behold, he consecrated it unconditionally, for everyone.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:3.hebrew: לפיכך - הואיל ויש בה מעילה, יש בה פדיון ויצאה לחולין, דהוי כשאר הקדש:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:3.english: Therefore - Since [the law of] misuse of consecrated property applies to it, redemption applies to it and it goes out to non-sacred status, for it is like other consecrated property.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:4.hebrew: אמר זו עלי הקדיש - כיון דאמר עלי, עליה דידיה שוויה הקדש, והוא מעל — אם אכל, חייב לשלומי:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:4.english: [If] he said, "This [is] upon me [as] consecrated [property]" - Since he said "upon me," he rendered it consecrated [only] with respect to himself, and he commits me'ilah [misuse of consecrated property] — if he ate [it], he is obligated to pay.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:5.hebrew: חבירו לא מעל - דלא אסרה אלא על עצמו, וגבי חבירו הוי כחולין:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:5.english: Another did not misuse [consecrated property] - For he forbade it only upon himself, and with respect to another it is like non-sacred [food].

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:6.hebrew: לפיכך אין לה פדיון - שהוא עצמו אין יכול לפדותה לעולם, שהרי אמר עלי ולא על אחר, ואחר אין יכול למעול בה:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:6:6.english: Therefore, it has no redemption - For he himself can never redeem it, since he said "for me" and not for another, and another cannot commit misuse with it.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:7:1.hebrew: בין כך ובין כך - בין אמר סתם, בין אמר עלי, לא מעל, בין הוא ובין חבירו. אף על פי שאמר הקדש, כיון דאמר נמי קונם, שאין מעילה בקונמות:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:7:1.english: Whether in this manner or in that manner - Whether he said [it] without specification or whether he said "for me," there is no misuse [of consecrated property], whether [by] him or [by] another. Even though he said "consecrated property," since he also said "konam," [there is no misuse,] because there is no misuse in konamot.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:8:1.english: Who misused [consecrated property] - He is asking according to the one who says there is misuse [of consecrated property] with konamot.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:8:2.english: It is not forbidden to him - [Referring] to the giver.

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:8:3.english: It is pleasing to me that you give me a permitted [item]; I did not want a forbidden [item] - That is to say, I received it from you in the status of a permitted [item], and not in the status of a forbidden [item].

Rashi on Nedarim 35a:8:4.hebrew: וכסבור של חולין הן מעל - אעפ"כ, הכי נמי אף זה המקבל — אע"פ שסבור זה המקבל שהיתר הוא, כי אכלה מעל:
Rashi on Nedarim 35a:8:4.english: And [when] he thinks that they are non-sacred, he commits misuse - Even so! So too [for] this recipient: even though this recipient thinks that it is permitted, when he eats it, he commits misuse.

Tosafot on Nedarim 35a:1:1.hebrew: קונם פרה שיש לי שאני הנאה לך נכסי עליך אם יש לי פרה אלא זו - שני נדרים הוו, ואי קאמר שאומר לו: "קונם פרה שיש לי שאוכל ליהנות לך ממנה", כלו' שאין לי פרה אחרת, ואם יש לי — תהא קונם עליך; או שאמר בלשון הזה: "נכסי עליך קונם אם יש לי פרה אלא זו שאני עושה בה מלאכתי", ונמצא שיש לו פרה אחרת, ועתה נאסרה הפרה והנכסים עליו. וגבי קונם נמי ה"פ כדפירשתי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 35a:1:1.english: Konam is any cow that I have from which I [provide] benefit to you; my property [is forbidden] to you if I have a cow other than this one - These are two [separate] vows. And if [the case is] that he says to him: "Konam is any cow that I have from which I can benefit you" — meaning, "I have no other cow, and if I do have [another], let it be konam to you" — or if he said in this language: "My property is konam to you if I have a cow other than this one with which I do my work," and it is found that he has another cow, then now the cow and the property become forbidden to him. And regarding [the second] konam [case] as well, this is its explanation, as I have explained.

Tosafot on Nedarim 35a:1:2.hebrew: מת או שנתנה לו במתנה מותרת - מת, דתו לא מיקרו פרה וקרדום שלו, וכן שנתנה לו במתנה מותרת. וקס"ד שנתנה המדיר למודר, ומשני שניתנה לו על ידי אחר. לפירוש שני דלעיל ניחא דפריך מנתנה לו במתנה, דאפרה ואקרדום קאי, ואע"ג דלא אמר "עליך"; אבל לפי' ראשון דלעיל דדייק מ"עליך", קשה: מאי פריך מנתנה לו פרה וקרדום? הא לא אמר "עליך"! וי"ל דלפי פירוש ראשון גרס "שניתנו" לשון רבים, וקאי נמי אנכסים. ודוחק הוא, שבכל הספרים גרסי' "שניתן" לשון יחיד, דמשמע דקאי דוקא אפרה ואקרדום; לכ"נ כפירוש שני. וא"ת: אכתי היא גופה תקשה לך, אמאי לא תנא "שניתנו" משום נכסים, הלא מיירי משנה גם מנכסים? וי"ל: מ"מ לא נחת לאשמועינן לאשריותא דפרה וקרדום, שהיה רוצה לישאל ממנו היה עיקר הנדר, וגם בכלל נכסים הם דמיתסר נמי בנדר כנכסים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 35a:1:2.english: [If the vower] died or it was given to him as a gift, it is permitted - [If he] died, [it is permitted] because they are no longer called his cow and spade, and likewise if it was given to him as a gift, it is permitted. And [the Gemara] initially assumed that the vower gave it to the subject of the vow, and [later] answers that it was given to him by another person. According to the second explanation above, it is understandable why [the Gemara] raises an objection from "it was given to him as a gift," for it refers to the cow and the spade, even though he did not say "to you"; however, according to the first explanation above, which infers from [the word] "to you," it is difficult: how can [the Gemara] raise an objection from "a cow or spade was given to him," when he did not say "to you"? And one can answer that according to the first explanation, one reads "that they were given" (shenitnu), in the plural, so that it also refers to "property." Yet this is forced, because in all the texts we read "that it was given" (shenitan), in the singular, which implies that it refers specifically to the cow or the spade; therefore, the second explanation appears [correct]. And if you ask: still, this itself should be a difficulty for you — why did [the Baraita] not teach "that they were given" on account of "property," since the Mishnah [i.e., the Baraita] also deals with "property"? And one can answer: in any event, [the Tanna] only came to teach us regarding the permitting of the cow and the spade, [since] what he wanted to borrow from him was the main subject of the vow, and they are also included in "property," so that they too are forbidden by the vow like property:

Tosafot on Nedarim 35a:6:1.hebrew: הוא מעל וחבירו לא מעל לפיכך אין לו פדיון וחכ"א בין כך ובין כך לא מעל - פירוש: וחכמים לא קאי לרישא אלא קאי לסיפא, דבעי למימר: בין הוא בין חבירו לא מעל. וקשה, דלישנא ד"בין כך ובין כך" משמע דקאי לכולה מלתא דר"מ. ועוד, משמע דאפילו לר"מ דיש בו מעילה, מכל מקום אין לו פדיון; וקשה, בפרק האשה רבה (יבמות דף פח.) משמע: האי יש בו מעילה, משום דבידו לפדותו — אלמא משמע דיש בו פדיה בקונמות! וע"ק: ברישא קאמר "ככר זה הקדש — מעל"; מאי קמשמע לן? פשיטא דהקדש גמור יש בו פדיון ומעילה! לכ"נ לפרש: דרישא לא מיירי בהקדש ממש, אלא בקונם בלשון הקדש, שאסר הככר לכל כמו הקדש; ולכך יש בו מעילה, כיון שנאסר לכל כהקדש גמור. "ככר זה עלי הקדש" — דמיירי בקונם שאינו אסור לכ"ע אלא לדידיה, לכך אין לו פדיון; דהא דאמרינן בשיש בו מעילה משום שבידו לפדותו, היינו קונם שאסור לכל כמו הקדש. וחכמים אומרים "בין כך ובין כך" כו' — קאי אפילו לרישא, משום דאין מעילה בשום קונמות; וכיון שאמר "הקדש" בלשון קונמות, אין מועלין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 35a:6:1.english: He misused consecrated property, while his fellow did not misuse consecrated property; therefore, it has no redemption. And the Sages say: Either way, he did not misuse consecrated property - Explanation: [One might initially think that] "the Sages" does not refer to the first clause, rather it refers to the latter clause, meaning to say: whether he or his fellow [ate it], he did not misuse consecrated property. However, this is difficult, for the wording "either way" implies that it refers to the entire statement of Rabbi Meir. Furthermore, it implies that even according to Rabbi Meir, where there is misuse of consecrated property, nevertheless it has no redemption; yet this is difficult, [for] in the chapter HaIsha Rabbah (Yevamot 88a) it is implied [that] the reason there is misuse of consecrated property is because it is in his power to redeem it — thus it implies that there is redemption for konamot! And furthermore, it is difficult: in the first clause it states, "[If one said,] 'This loaf is consecrated property,' he misused consecrated property" — what is it teaching us? It is obvious that full-fledged consecrated property has redemption and misuse of consecrated property! Therefore, it appears [correct] to explain that the first clause is not speaking of actual consecrated property, rather of a konam [vow] using the language of consecrated property, where he prohibited the loaf to everyone like consecrated property; and therefore there is misuse of consecrated property in it, since it was prohibited to everyone like full-fledged consecrated property. [And the latter clause,] "This loaf is consecrated property upon me" — which speaks of a konam that is not prohibited to everyone, rather only to himself — therefore it has no redemption; for that which we say that wherever there is misuse of consecrated property it is because it is in his power to redeem it, that applies to a konam that is prohibited to everyone like consecrated property. And [as for] "the Sages say: Either way, etc." — it refers even to the first clause, because there is no misuse of consecrated property in any konamot; and since he said "consecrated property" in the language of konamot, they do not commit misuse of consecrated property.
